headings.title: SMTO-CAP-0003 — SMTO looked for a part of a Skill that doesn't exist

html:
SMTO-CAP-0003 — SMTO looked for a part of a Skill that doesn't exist

GUID: 7bd4c122-4fef-4b9a-8e0d-a936b30ebc2a
Slug: unknown-section
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • While working on your Task, SMTO's Agent asked for a section of a Skill that isn't in that Skill's list. Nothing was run, and the Agent usually picks a real section and carries on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the Task for a moment. If it keeps working after this message, you don't need to do anything. SMTO tells the Agent which sections the Skill really has, so the Agent can correct the name by itself.
  2. If the Task stops, open Capabilities by the message box, select Refresh catalog, and check the Skill is listed and not marked Unavailable. A Skill that was just updated or removed may no longer have the section the Agent remembered.
  3. Ask SMTO to continue the Task, and say in plain words which Skill you want it to use. Naming the Skill helps the Agent start from that Skill's real list of sections instead of guessing.

What success looks like

  • The Task moves past the capability step and keeps working without this message.

If it still fails

  • Open Technical details, select Copy error details, and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they show the exact section name the Agent asked for. Don't keep sending the same request unchanged, because it will look for the same missing section.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Capability discovery (discover_tools) rejected a section_id that is not in the selected Skill's registered section tree (error kind unknown_section); no tool was advertised or executed.

What this means

  • Capability discovery could not find the requested section in the selected skill's registered API tree. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Capability discovery could not find the requested section in the selected skill's registered API tree.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested section ID with the skill's current section list, including parent/child structure.

How to fix it

  • Compare the requested section_id with the Skill's current sections returned by discover_tools(skill_ids=[...]) (ToolCatalog._discover in src/agent_runtime/native/catalog.py) and request an exact listed section. If the Skill was updated or removed, update or reinstall it on /skills so its section tree matches what the Agent was told.
  • Refresh the current capability sections and choose an exact existing section.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Discovery accepts an exact currently registered section and returns its allowed tools.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
